The upper triangle zeroing happens per-row after completion but is never read by other computations since all reads stay within the lower triangle, so there's no conflict there.\n\nFor non-positive-definite errors, I need the parallel version to match sequential behavior: the reported failure must be the smallest row index i where the diagonal check fails, even though later rows may compute concurrently. I can handle this with an atomic flag or min-tracking so threads stop reporting once a failure is detected, ensuring only the earliest failing index gets printed.\n\nSo the dependency chain confirms that whenever row i's diagonal computation fails, every earlier row i' < i must have already had its diagonal computed, since (i,i) transitively depends on those values through the sum terms. This guarantees the first error encountered corresponds to the smallest failing index.\n\nThat said, a failure at some i' > i could technically be detected first if its computation happens to finish sooner, so simply tracking which thread hits NaN or division-by-zero first isn't reliable -- I need an atomic minimum over all failing indices and report that at the end, while also worrying about downstream threads consuming already-corrupted values like NaN results propagating further.\n\nSince any earlier row is an ancestor of any later row, the ancestor already got checked and recorded before the later one, so the first recorded failure is guaranteed to be the global minimum. To be safe though, I'll still track the minimum failing row with an atomic compare-exchange rather than relying purely on first-failure ordering.\n\nI'm also confirming that rows before the true failure point only ever depend on valid inputs, so parallel execution computes them identically to sequential, and if the matrix gets partially modified after a failure that's fine since the sequential version doesn't print anything either in that case. Now I'm thinking through scheduling options for parallelizing row-by-row, starting with a dynamic approach using atomic counters to track progress per row.\n\nI'm working out the dependency constraints: for off-diagonal entries, a row needs earlier rows' diagonal values finalized before computing, so threads must wait on a progress counter per row reaching at least the diagonal column plus one. I'm also checking whether the zeroing of upper-triangular entries after a row completes could interfere with readers, but since readers only access columns up to their own index, this shouldn't cause conflicts.\n\nFor memory ordering I'm reasoning through using atomic progress counters with release/acquire semantics so writes are visible before the counter updates, and considering using OpenMP's dynamic scheduling with chunk size 1 so rows are always dispatched in increasing order, avoiding deadlocks since dependent rows start before the rows that need them.\n\nThe critical-path analysis shows each row's progress lags behind earlier rows naturally due to the dependency structure, and the total work scales roughly quadratically per row from the dot-product computations, so the wavefront parallelism is bounded but deadlock-free.\n\nTotal work scales like n^3/6 multiply-adds while the critical path scales like n^2/2, giving a parallelism ratio on the order of n, which suggests decent but not perfect scalability for large n.\n\nI can cache the progress check locally since it's monotone, so each element only needs an atomic load when the cached value is insufficient—roughly n²/2 total loads, negligible against n³/6 flops. The bigger worry is false sharing: each row writes its own progress counter after every column, so adjacent counters on the same cache line get hammered by different threads reading and writing, causing ping-pong contention.\n\nThinking through the actual dependency more carefully, a reader at column c really just needs row c itself to be fully finished through its own diagonal entry before anyone downstream can use it.\n\nSo each row only needs one \"done\" flag rather than fine-grained per-column signals, since row c finalizes right at its last column. But that reduces pipelining: row i can't touch column j until row j is entirely complete, meaning the critical path becomes essentially sequential across rows rather than finer-grained.\n\nTracking the completed-rows frontier F, row i can progress through columns up to F before stalling, so many rows advance in lockstep bounded by that frontier rather than independently.\n\nOverall the total time likely lands around the sum of the diagonal chain, roughly n²/2 operations, bounded against total work divided by processors, with theoretical parallelism around n/3 since rows can overlap with some lag between them.\n\nBut I'm now worried about threads spin-waiting: within a row, waiting on a column's dependency means idle cycles if that column's row hasn't finished yet. Since the dot product itself is inherently sequential (can't reorder the k-sum without changing numerical results), parallelizing within a row's computation isn't really viable while preserving exact semantics.\n\nI'm also considering whether a right-looking formulation could avoid the dependency chain, but that changes the order of floating-point subtraction and would break bit-exact reproducibility. I'd rather keep the straightforward sequential summation to guarantee identical output hashes, even if it costs performance.\n\nThe matrix generation step (the n³ matmul B*Bᵀ) isn't timed, only the decomposition is, so parallelizing that part doesn't matter. The real parallel granularity is at the row level with dependency tracking, since elements within a row depend sequentially on earlier ones in that row.\n\nI can still safely parallelize the B*Bᵀ generation and the final validation matmul since both preserve summation order per element, and the max-error check is order-independent too, so that's an easy win for overall runtime without affecting correctness. But I realize waiters spinning on done[j] need to also check the failed flag, otherwise they'd hang forever if row j itself failed instead of completing—so the wait loop needs to abort on failure, not just completion.\n\nFor the failure message, I should print it once after the parallel region using the recorded failRow, keeping wording identical to the sequential version. Since multiple rows could fail concurrently, I need an atomic min (compare-exchange loop) to track the minimum failing row safely rather than assuming only one failure happens.\n\nThe upper-triangle zeroing in each row only needs to finish before that row's done-flag is set, since no reader ever touches upper elements anyway - diagonal and off-diagonal reads both stay in the lower triangle, so there's no actual dependency issue there. For thread count I'll just rely on OpenMP's default of using all available cores for maximum scalability, with standard scheduling, and note that first-touch NUMA effects depend on how generation initializes the matrix in main.\n\nFor the spin-wait on dependencies, I'll have threads check an atomic \"done\" flag with acquire ordering and a failure flag, pausing or yielding briefly between checks rather than busy-spinning aggressively — this should be safe since the number of active rows never exceeds the thread count. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793058286053,"sessionID":"ses_e856779ebffe4xQY10e7wd0toP","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01V9aw8daMm5ZgPpg92dLg5h","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <omp.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <atomic>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <memory>\n#include <thread>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Parallel Cholesky decomposition (OpenMP, unblocked row-oriented algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// Parallelization strategy:\n//   - Row i of L depends only on the finished rows j < i (their lower parts).\n//     Each row is one task; rows are handed out in increasing order via\n//     dynamic scheduling, so any row a task waits for has already been started.\n//   - Row j is published as finished through an atomic flag (release/acquire),\n//     which makes its values visible to the rows that consume them.\n//   - Every dot product is accumulated in exactly the same order as the\n//     sequential algorithm, so the results are bit-identical to it.\n//   - If a diagonal element is not positive, the row that failed is the lowest\n//     failing row (all earlier rows were completed before it can be reached),\n//     which is reported exactly as in the sequential version.\n\n// Wait until row is finished. Returns false if a failure was signalled meanwhile.\nstatic inline bool waitForRow(const std::atomic<bool>& rowDone, const std::atomic<bool>& failed) {\n    unsigned int spins = 0;\n    while (!rowDone.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {\n        if (failed.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (++spins > 64) {\n            std::this_thread::yield();\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n\n    std::unique_ptr<std::atomic<bool>[]> rowDone(new std::atomic<bool>[n]);\n    for (size_t r = 0; r < n; ++r) {\n        rowDone[r].store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);\n    }\n\n    std::atomic<bool> failed{false};\n    std::atomic<size_t> failedRow{n};\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        if (failed.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        double* const Ai = a + i * n;\n        bool ok = true;\n\n        // Off-diagonal elements of row i\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) {\n            if (!waitForRow(rowDone[j], failed)) {\n                ok = false;\n                break;\n            }\n            const double* const Aj = a + j * n;\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += Ai[k] * Aj[k];\n            }\n            Ai[j] = (Ai[j] - sum) / Aj[j];\n        }\n\n        if (!ok) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Diagonal element of row i\n        {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < i; ++k) {\n                sum += Ai[k] * Ai[k];\n            }\n            const double val = Ai[i] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                size_t expected = n;\n                failedRow.compare_exchange_strong(expected, i, std::memory_order_relaxed);\n                failed.store(true, std::memory_order_release);\n                continue;\n            }\n            Ai[i] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n\n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            Ai[j] = 0.0;\n        }\n\n        rowDone[i].store(true, std::memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    if (failed.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", failedRow.load());\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B (sequential: the random sequence must be preserved)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T (rows are independent)\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T (rows are independent)\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static) reduction(max : maxError, relError)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793058285936,"end":1793058286003}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17a9a0414001FK2kfUYKru3m6f","sessionID":"ses_e856779ebffe4xQY10e7wd0toP","messageID":"msg_17a99f883001imIkbwzSPegfVe"}}
